New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A new wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery.
  • Industry observers note that known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time.
  • REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A new wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery. Developed by researchers led by the University of Texas at Austin, the device uses gentle ultrasound waves to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, helping people enter REM sleep sooner and spend more time in this restorative stage.

Industry observers note that known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time. This allows researchers to influence brain regions involved in sleep while simultaneously tracking how the brain responds.

REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs. It also plays an important role in processing emotions, consolidating memories, and adapting to stress. Disturbances in this stage of sleep have been associated with several mental health conditions, making it an important target for upcoming treatments.

Industry observers note that "This is the first time we've been able to noninvasively target deep brain regions involved in REM sleep, while simultaneously monitoring brain activity," said Kai Wing "Kevin" Tang, a recent UT biomedical engineering Ph.D. graduate who led the research effort.

"Our skin-attached NEUSLeeP patch opens up newly introduced possibilities for understanding sleep and treating sleep disorders in home settings," added Huiliang "Evan" Wang, assistant professor in the Cockrell School of Engineering's Department of Biomedical Engineering. Wang supervised Tang's research and served as the principal investigator (PI) overseeing the project.

Sleep Patch Helps People Reach REM Sleep 43 Minutes Faster.

The early results suggest that the technology can make a measurable difference in how people experience REM sleep.

In a study involving 28 participants, published in Nature Communications, people using the patch entered REM sleep an average of 43 minutes sooner and spent approximately 16 additional minutes in that stage.

These improvements were observed in both healthy sleepers and participants experiencing certain sleep difficulties. The volunteers also reported that the patch was comfortable to wear, with minimal adverse effects.

In a recent development, unlike medications that affect the body more broadly, NEUSLeeP is designed to deliver stimulation to specific brain regions involved in sleep regulation. It uses ultrasound, a form of sound energy with frequencies beyond human hearing, to reach areas beneath the surface of the brain without requiring an invasive procedure.

The findings are encouraging, although the relatively small study means that larger trials will be needed to determine how consistently the technology works and whether its benefits persist over time.

Potential Benefits for Stress and Emotional Health.

The researchers also found evidence that the patch's effects may extend beyond increasing REM sleep.

Among healthy participants, ultrasound stimulation improved heart rate variability, a measure of the natural differences in time between consecutive heartbeats. This measurement provides insight into how the body's nervous system responds to stress and adjusts to changing conditions.

In a recent development, brain imaging revealed changes in neural circuits involved in emotional processing. Together, these findings suggest that improving REM sleep through targeted stimulation could potentially support emotional regulation and the ability to cope with stress.

Recent findings suggest that "REM sleep is not just about dreaming -- it's about emotional reset and stress adaptation," explained Gregory Fonzo, assistant professor in the Dell Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and one of the project's co-PIs. "By enhancing REM, we may help people better cope with stress and improve their overall well-being.".

These possibilities are especially interesting because REM sleep disturbances have been linked to depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

Current approaches to sleep problems often involve medication or behavioral therapy. Although these treatments can be effective, medications may produce unwanted side effects, and existing approaches do not always directly address the biological processes responsible for disrupted REM sleep.

Recent findings suggest that A device capable of influencing those processes without drugs or surgery could therefore offer an additional treatment option. However, the researchers have not yet established whether NEUSLeeP can improve symptoms of mental health disorders.

A New Direction for Treating Insomnia and PTSD.

Building on the initial findings, the research team intends to conduct larger clinical trials to confirm the patch's effects and investigate its potential use in people with PTSD, depression, and chronic insomnia.

Beyond treating sleep disorders, the technology could eventually support sleep monitoring at home and provide scientists with a fresh way to study how deep brain regions influence sleep. Researchers also envision personalized therapies that could be adjusted to individual sleep patterns and needs.

In a recent development, "Our vision is a future where patients with mental health disorders can optimize their sleep with a noninvasive and safe treatment," noted Vincent Mysliwiec, M.D., a professor at UT Health San Antonio, a leading expert in sleep disorders, and another co-PI on the project. "This technology could help millions of people get the restorative sleep they need.".

According to recent reports, the team is already taking steps toward making NEUSLeeP available beyond the research setting. Working with the university's commercialization unit, Discovery to Impact, the researchers are exploring how to bring the device to market and have filed a patent application covering the technology.

If future studies confirm the early results, this wearable ultrasound patch could become a valuable upcoming tool for improving REM sleep and potentially addressing conditions associated with poor sleep.

Industry observers note that other members of the research team include William D. Moscoso-Barrera, Mengxia Yu, Mengmeng Yao, Jinmo Jeong, Ilya Pyatnitskiy, Anakaren Romero Lozano, Jiachen Wang, Ju-Chun Hsieh, Tony Sungjin Chae, Daniel Song, Julieta Garcia, Rithvik Mittapalli, and Adam Bush of the Department of Biomedical Engineering; Benjamin Baird of the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Psychology; and Wynn Legon of Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia, the upcoming cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a massive launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

In a recent development, the developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing upcoming inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

It has been revealed that the game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Recent findings suggest that whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, updated on November 19th, 2026 - reformatted and rechecked the list With GTA VI now finally in the hands of players, a decade-plus wait is finally over.
  • According to recent reports, well, that's where we come in, with our list of the best mobile games like Grand Theft Auto; covering a huge variety of open-world, crime-focused action games.
  • It has been revealed that yes, while Grove Street Games' mobile ports may be considered a bit lacklustre by some, they're still well-loved for bringing some of the greatest console classics to mobile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, updated on November 19th, 2026 - reformatted and rechecked the list With GTA VI now finally in the hands of players, a decade-plus wait is finally over. But what if you're going to be without your console or PC for a while? How exactly do you get that hit of open-world action when you can't find GTA VI on mobile (yet)?

According to recent reports, well, that's where we come in, with our list of the best mobile games like Grand Theft Auto; covering a huge variety of open-world, crime-focused action games. And, luckily enough, plenty of the classic GTAs are also already on mobile!

It has been revealed that yes, while Grove Street Games' mobile ports may be considered a bit lacklustre by some, they're still well-loved for bringing some of the greatest console classics to mobile. And we'll get to them in due course!

Arguably the only 'true' competitor to Grand Theft Auto that saw any measure of success near their level, Saints Row always dove into the wackier, stranger and more glitzy sides of street culture. And with the Third Street Saints ditching their humble origins, when they're brought back to earth, it's up to you to once more become kings of crime in the brand-new city of Steelport.

Whether it's flopping off of car hoods to defraud insurance, battling zombies with an oversized marital aid or simply speeding through the air on your jet-bike (Volition did it first), Saints Row: The Third offers exciting open-world crime action on mobile that's almost on par with the best GTA has to offer.

A real gem of Rockstar's back catalogue, when it seemed as if they always had something experimental up their sleeve before their attention turned solely to Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption. Bully: Anniversary Edition is a game that was massively controversial as well as beloved by fans.

Set in Bullworth Academy, you play reckless delinquent Jimmy as you navigate the various social cliques, overbearing administration and tedious lessons inflicted on you. And along the way, maybe, just maybe, you'll turn the world of Bullworth upside down in a way no one will forget.

When Rockstar decided they wanted to dust off their quirky, spaghetti-western shooter Red Dead Revolver and give it a brand-new GTA-style makeover, I think few expected it to be as popular as it became.

Sources indicate that playing as John Marston, you'll ride the range of the American West in pursuit of your former comrades-in-crime, with the intent of saving your family and maybe your own soul along the way. Expect shootouts, bank robberies, cattle rustling and maybe a few zombies along the way.

One of many GTA Online-likes to try and recreate the open-world crime experience on mobile, just with fewer Shark Cards, Grand Outlaws is another recent release well worth looking into. While its more colourful setting may clash with what you expect from a gritty crime thriller, and it looks more Fortnite than Sleeping Dogs, it's still got plenty of appeal for those wanting something GTA-style in their lives.

According to recent reports, probably one of the largest-scale competitors in the GTA Online-likes scene, OneState is one to go for if you prefer a more realistic interpretation of open-world crime and action than Grand Outlaws. Its realistic recreation of Los Angeles even boasts a near-future, plausible version of real-life developments.

About the only thing to be aware of when it comes to OneState is that this is an RP game first and foremost, and you'll be just as likely to fall into the role of firefighter or EMT as a crime kingpin. But if that depth of realism is what you're hunting for, OneState is sure to satisfy.

A really unique (as much as my editors hate using that word) entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, Chinatown Wars takes you back to Liberty City. But rather than exploring the mafia connections, you'll be joining the deadly world of the triads.

Set from a top-down perspective like the classic entries in the series, Chinatown Wars boasts interesting minigames, the same level of violence and chaos as you'd expect, as well as a sprawling narrative of revenge and ambition.

According to recent reports, download now! Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars Max Payne.

Are we breaking from the trend of 'open world' here? Sure, absolutely. But Max Payne, first released by Remedy and later acquired by Rockstar, is undoubtedly full of the same gunplay and thrilling crime storylines as any GTA entry. And, I'd argue, that its actual gunplay is leagues ahead of what Grand Theft Auto has ever offered.

Set in New York during the middle of a snowstorm, you play as the gritty police detective Max Payne as you shoot your way through hordes of mafia goons. The bullet-time mechanic still holds up years later, and if you need a short, sharp hit of shootout action, then Max Payne is one to grab.

Download now! Max Payne Mobile Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories.

Another one-off entry in the brief portable series that Rockstar had, which includes Vice City Stories (sadly not available on mobile). In Liberty City Stories, you return once more to the 3D incarnation of their New York analogue, before it got a major makeover for Grand Theft Auto IV.

Playing as Toni Cipriani, you'll be working closely with the mafia and experience Liberty City and what it was like before Grand Theft Auto III. Definitely one to play if you were a fan of watching The Sopranos, and if you're just a big fan of delving into the history of GTA as a universe!

And now for something completely different... Okay, not that different. But Neverness to Everness is undoubtedly one to play only if you're willing to really stretch the definition of a GTA-like. Rather than a realistic city or characters, you'll be jumping into anime-inspired action with flashy combat and a sprawling metropolis.

Recent findings suggest that but even if you are fighting on the right side of the law, Neverness to Everness tries to lean into the mayhem of GTA just as much as any other. And while it's had some controversial issues with AI, at its core it's still got plenty of the same fun to be had on the go as Grand Theft Auto.

It has been revealed that A Gameloft production for mobile, Gangstar Vegas may be the lesser pick on this list. But, purely for curiosity's sake it's well worth looking at for its ambition alone. Released back in 2013, Gangstar Vegas was arguably the first mobile game to try and match what GTA had to offer, full 3D world included.

According to recent reports, boasting all the same glitz, glamour and grime as GTA, not to mention the always-fun Las Vegas setting, Gangstar Vegas: World of Crime is rightly regarded as a flawed, but lovable cult classic that really shows how difficult it is to pin down the formula. Still, it gets more than a few points for trying.

Download now! Gangstar Vegas Honourable Mention: Other GTA Ports If what you want is just GTA, name included, then mobile is pretty chock-a-block with them. We've got Vice City, San Andreas, Chinatown Wars and Grand Theft Auto III all available to play on your choice of iOS or Android. Not to mention the er, Definitive Edition ports too.

But, as you may well know, these are ports where a lot of rough edges can be seen. While not quite as shoddy as the infamous Definitive Collection, Grove Street Games' ports of the original 3D trilogy are definitely not the best way to experience them, but on mobile they're all feature-complete and almost as good as you remember them; keyword being 'almost'. And with that in mind, those are some of the best, if not the best, ways to experience GTA-like action on mobile while you're away from your console or PC! And if you want to relive the classics, you've also got options with the available ports. So, when you need to take a break from GTA VI, you're still spoilt for choice on mobile.

#17728. Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1516 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits.
  • According to recent reports, researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease.
  • The results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits. Although heavy drinking was linked to worse health outcomes regardless of the beverage, the picture was more complicated among people who consumed smaller amounts of alcohol.

According to recent reports, researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease. In contrast, similar amounts of beer, cider, and spirits were linked to a higher risk. The findings, presented at the American College of Cardiology's Annual Scientific Session (ACC.26), suggest that both the type and quantity of alcohol may influence its relationship with long-term health.

The results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health. Importantly, the new findings do not establish that wine itself protects against disease.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," remarked Zhangling Chen, MD, PhD, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author.

How a Study of 340,000 Adults Measured Alcohol Risk.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate the relationship between drinking habits and longevity, scientists examined data from 340,924 adults enrolled in the UK Biobank between 2006 and 2022. The UK Biobank is a large research resource that collects health and lifestyle information to help scientists investigate factors associated with disease and mortality.

Participants reported their alcohol consumption through dietary questionnaires when they joined the study. Researchers then classified them into four groups based on how much pure alcohol they typically consumed each day or week, rather than simply counting drinks.

Industry observers note that this distinction matters because beer, wine, and spirits contain different concentrations of alcohol. For comparison, a 12-ounce can of beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of spirits each provide approximately 14 grams of pure alcohol.

Industry observers note that people consuming fewer than 20 g (about 1.5 standard drinks) per week were placed in the never or occasional drinking group. Low consumption was defined as 20 g per week up to 20 g per day for men, and 20 g per week up to 10 g per day for women.

According to recent reports, moderate drinking was defined as 20 g to 40 g (about 1.5 to three standard drinks) daily for men and 10 g to 20 g daily for women. High consumption meant more than 40 g (about three drinks) per day for men or more than 20 g (about 1.5 drinks) per day for women.

Researchers followed participants' health outcomes for an average of more than 13 years, allowing them to examine how drinking patterns were associated with deaths from different causes.

Wine, Beer, and Spirits Show Different Heart Health Risks.

Industry observers note that the clearest finding concerned heavy alcohol consumption. Compared with people who never drank or consumed alcohol only occasionally, heavy drinkers had a 24% higher risk of dying from any cause. Their risk of dying from cancer was 36% higher, while their risk of dying from heart disease was 14% higher.

These increased risks were associated with heavy drinking regardless of whether participants preferred wine, beer, cider, or spirits.

However, the results became more surprising when researchers examined low and moderate alcohol consumption. At these levels, the type of beverage was associated with substantially different outcomes.

People who consumed wine in low to moderate amounts had a significantly lower risk of death, while those who consumed comparable amounts of beer, cider, or spirits had a significantly higher risk.

The contrast was especially striking for cardiovascular disease, a broad category of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease than people who never or only occasionally drank alcohol.

By comparison, even low consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was associated with a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

According to recent reports, these percentages describe relative differences in risk between groups, not the absolute probability that an individual will die from cardiovascular disease. Because the research was observational, the findings also cannot demonstrate that choosing one alcoholic beverage over another directly changes a person's risk.

"Our findings help clarify previously mixed evidence on low to moderate alcohol consumption," Chen mentioned. "These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed, but also on the type of beverage. Even low to moderate intake of spirits, beer, or cider is linked to higher mortality, while low to moderate intake of wine may carry lower risk.".

Why Might Wine Be Linked to Lower Heart Risks?

Researchers identified several possible explanations for the differences, including the chemical composition of wine and the habits of people who drink it.

Red wine contains polyphenols, naturally occurring compounds found in plants that can have antioxidant properties. Antioxidants help counter certain chemical reactions involving unstable molecules that can damage cells. Some polyphenols have been investigated for potential benefits to blood vessels and cardiovascular function.

These compounds could contribute to the associations observed in wine drinkers, although the study did not establish that they were responsible for the lower mortality risk.

Another possible explanation involves how and when people drink.

Wine is more commonly consumed alongside meals, and wine drinkers often report healthier diets and lifestyle habits. Drinking wine may therefore be associated with other behaviors that support cardiovascular health.

According to recent reports, beer, cider, and spirits, on the other hand, are more frequently consumed outside of meals. In this study, people who favored these beverages also tended to have poorer overall diet quality and other lifestyle factors associated with increased health risks.

Such differences make it difficult to separate the effects of the alcohol itself from the characteristics and habits of the people consuming it.

"Taken together, these factors suggest that the type of alcohol, how it is consumed, and the associated lifestyle behaviors all contribute to the observed differences in mortality risk," Chen remarked.

What the Findings Mean for Alcohol and Health.

Recent findings suggest that to make their comparisons more reliable, the researchers statistically adjusted their analyses for numerous factors that might influence mortality. These included age and other demographic characteristics, socioeconomic circumstances, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic health.

In a recent development, cardiometabolic factors include conditions and measurements related to heart and metabolic health, such as blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, and cholesterol levels. The analyses also accounted for family histories of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

Even with these adjustments, the researchers emphasized several important limitations.

It has been revealed that because the study was observational, it could identify associations between alcohol consumption and mortality but could not prove that particular beverages caused better or worse outcomes. Other differences between participants may have influenced the findings despite the statistical adjustments.

It has been revealed that alcohol intake was also measured through questionnaires completed when participants first entered the study. That information depended on participants accurately reporting their own drinking habits, and it did not capture changes in consumption during the years that followed.

In a recent development, another consideration is that UK Biobank participants tend to be healthier than the general population. This could limit how well the findings apply to other groups of people.

Sources indicate that the researchers suggested that high-quality randomized trials could provide stronger evidence about the health effects of different drinking patterns. Such studies would help clarify whether the observed differences reflect the beverages themselves or other factors associated with their consumption.

Nevertheless, the enormous study population and more than 13 years of average follow-up provide considerable statistical strength. By examining specific types of alcohol, different levels of consumption, and multiple causes of death, the research offers a more detailed picture of alcohol's potential health risks than many earlier investigations.

The findings highlight an vital distinction: while heavy drinking is consistently associated with harmful health outcomes, the relationships observed at lower consumption levels may depend on beverage choice, drinking habits, and broader lifestyle patterns.

For now, the apparent advantage among wine drinkers should not be interpreted as a reason to start drinking wine for heart health. The evidence points to a complex relationship between alcohol and mortality, rather than proving that any alcoholic drink offers protection.

Ziyue Li presented the study, "Alcohol Use at Mid-Life and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality," at ACC.26.

Capcom is bringing Mega Man: Dual Override to the Switch 1 & 2 in 2027 and to build some excitement, it's been revealing the Robot Masters you'll be facing in the game.

According to recent reports, this week it's officially revealed the sixth Robot Master, 'Boat Man'. Here's the official description, along with a look (via Rockman Corner):.

A coastal fishing robot with a timid nature, Boat Man drops anchor in Mega Man: Dual Override! Teased for being hesitant to venture the high seas, this nautical nemesis unleashes a typhoon of tyranny against all who doubt him!

Industry observers note that this follows Capcom announcing the winner of the Mega Man: Dual Override Robot Master design contest earlier this week. It's "Cleanser Man"!

These Robot Masters will be joined by Cook Man, Tank Man, Twinkle Girl and Jet Man, with more Robot Master Reveals to come.

Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG.
  • Recent findings suggest that as recently revealed, the new experience debuts today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT.
  • This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

Recent findings suggest that as recently revealed, the new experience debuts today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside patch 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

It has been revealed that the beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the proposal is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

It has been revealed that you need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

In a recent development, the Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two upcoming additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup.
  • The Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko.
  • Sources indicate that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup. The move pairs him again with former NRG teammate brawk as Sentinels try to return to international events after missing them all in 2026.

The Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Sources indicate that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

It has been revealed that sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and stated keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

In a recent development, the signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

It has been revealed that that spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko mentioned on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a newly introduced team as a restricted free agent.

According to recent reports, sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap quickly.

keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

The final piece has arrived, and he's bloody brilliant@Keikofps is officially a Sentinel pic.twitter.com/F5plGsyugj.

— Sentinels (@Sentinels) November 16, 2026.

The upcoming lineup’s next test is the Americas Kickoff. Partner teams are guaranteed a place only at Kickoff. The Americas has eight partner teams, and all of them receive direct invitations to its event. Four further places go to non-partner teams.

In a recent development, the 2027 Kickoff events will be played in person in each international region. One of the non-partner places in the Americas will be decided by a Last Chance Qualifier in São Paulo on 17–18 December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that chapter 5 of Toby Fox’s newest indie game opus, Deltarune, introduced back in June of this year.
  • It has been revealed that based on some little hints that Fox has previously dropped, Chapter 6 will be when the game starts reaching its narrative crux, bringing an end to “wacky silly adventures” in the face of all the mysteries that have been building up, and there are a lot of them.
  • In the newest edition of the Deltarune newsletter for Fall 2026, Fox revealed that Chapter 6 is “structurally complete,” in that you can technically play it from start to finish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chapter 5 of Toby Fox’s newest indie game opus, Deltarune, introduced back in June of this year. It’s kind of interesting to think about; when that chapter launched, it completely dominated the gaming sphere for a good month, even if it didn’t quite hit with everyone. Now that GTA 6 is out and completely taken over the scene, it’s gone largely quiet outside of its specific fanbase. Still, perhaps that’s for the best. A little less attention means that Fox and his team will have some extra breathing room as they work on the next stretch of the game, which is set to encompass both Chapter 6 and Chapter 7.

It has been revealed that based on some little hints that Fox has previously dropped, Chapter 6 will be when the game starts reaching its narrative crux, bringing an end to “wacky silly adventures” in the face of all the mysteries that have been building up, and there are a lot of them. It’s still going to be a while before we actually get to see any of this, mind you, but according to Fox, development is going pretty swimmingly.

In the newest edition of the Deltarune newsletter for Fall 2026, Fox revealed that Chapter 6 is “structurally complete,” in that you can technically play it from start to finish. The next orders of business will be to hammer out the nitty-gritty details, as well as get things rolling in earnest on Chapter 7.

As Fox explained in the newsletter, Chapter 6 is a “structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist,” though he parenthetically noted that there’s a particular optional event that’s causing the overall development to drag out a bit.

“By the time you read this, we should have started the localization and some preliminary testing. Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing,” Fox remarked.

Industry observers note that he admitted that, while Chapter 6 will be shorter in length than the previous chapters, it’s going to be a pivotal one, and he wants it to hit as hard as it possibly can. In short, this is not a process that can be rushed; it’ll only be ready once he’s satisfied with it.

By the time you read this, we should have started the localization and some preliminary testing.

On the bright side, thanks to a fan vote, Fox opted to share a brief sneak peek of Chapter 6 in the form of a quote unquote “stupid scene” involving Queen meeting with Pink in Castle Town and being… her Queenly self, let’s say. Hey, it made me laugh.

The newsletter also shared an revision on Chapter 7, though as Fox rather succinctly puts it, “Well, we've only just started…”.

While development on Chapter 7 has only just begun, Fox feels as though he’s on the right track with his team and their work. Apparently, the way they’re handling development is by having Fox read out the events and dialogue of the chapter to the team, then stopping just as the story reaches a critical point. The only way for the team to find out what happens next is for more of the game to be completed. A bit of an unusual approach, but apparently, “Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.”.

With so much of Deltarune already under the team’s belt, Fox is feeling optimistic as they all get started in earnest on Chapter 7. “Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!”.

Fox concluded the newsletter with a reminder that, as development on the game goes on, the dev team keeps getting bigger, which is why more time is needed to ensure everything comes out right.

“I know it's probably annoying to not have any updates, but no news is good news.”.

Whether you like it or loathe it, there's no doubting the popularity and staying power of Monopoly Go for Scopely. Now, the hit tabletop-to-mobile adaptation is receiving an all-new minigame. Paths challenge you to think cooperatively, or look out for yourself, and debut today with the launch of the new Franken Paths as part of the Monster Mash season!

Paths are a straightforward cooperative minigame where you and up to three other tycoons team up to build a path and move a shared vehicle along it. You'll accumulate points and have the choice to either use them to build your assigned portion (and reap the rewards) or send them to another player, with the aim of reaching the end together and getting even greater goodies.

In a recent development, admittedly though, I feel as if Scopely are trying a little too hard to sell the 'send or keep' message with Paths. I'm really only extrapolating whether there's any benefit to you actually keeping your points, and given the whole team is working together to reach each section, is there really any benefit to holding onto them?

Well, either way, it's a fun little addition, and the co-op aspect is sure to get people talking and playing. So if you're going to be jumping in, why not check out our Monopoly Go daily dice links for a few free boosts we've collated?

Industry News: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering important questions about its effects on mental health.
  • According to recent reports, published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition.
  • The findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering important questions about its effects on mental health. A major latest study suggests that people who struggle to control their cannabis use face a substantially greater likelihood of experiencing suicidal thoughts.

According to recent reports, published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition. Despite major shifts in marijuana laws and public attitudes, this troubling association remained remarkably consistent over a decade.

The findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Researchers examined data collected between 2014 and 2023, a period when cannabis became increasingly accessible across the United States.

"What surprised me most was not that cannabis use disorder was associated with suicidal thoughts, but that this association did not appear to strengthen over time," said lead author Tosin Philip Oyetunji, MPH, a doctoral student in public health at the University of California, Merced. "[Yet,] it remains an important mental health concern that deserves attention.".

Cannabis and Suicidal Thoughts Show a Persistent Link.

According to recent reports, the connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thinking was observed across different age groups, sexes, and racial and ethnic backgrounds. However, women and younger adults indicated particularly elevated risks.

Importantly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for depression, psychological distress, and other factors that could influence mental health outcomes.

According to recent reports, the consistency of the results was especially notable given how dramatically the cannabis landscape has changed. Recreational marijuana is now legal in half of U.S. states, and cannabis products have become increasingly potent. These developments have raised concerns among public health experts about whether broader access might contribute to worsening mental health.

Yet the study offers some reassurance on that particular question. Sidra Goldman-Mellor, PhD, a professor of public health at UC Merced and the study's senior author, noted that the association between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts did not become stronger during the 10 years examined.

It has been revealed that "Suicidal ideation does not seem to have increased among people with cannabis use disorder, despite all this legal and social change," explained Goldman-Mellor. Yet, "people with cannabis use disorder are still at a very substantially increased likelihood of experiencing serious suicidal thoughts, and that's not something that is widely understood.".

Why Cannabis Use Disorder Matters.

The researchers stress that these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that everyone who uses marijuana faces the same elevated risk.

Sources indicate that the study focused specifically on cannabis use disorder, a condition in which people have difficulty controlling their marijuana consumption even when it causes problems in their lives. Someone with the disorder may continue using cannabis despite harmful consequences or repeated attempts to cut back.

This distinction is important because problematic cannabis use differs from occasional or otherwise nonproblematic consumption.

Recent findings suggest that the findings also do not establish that cannabis use disorder directly causes suicidal thoughts. Because the research identified an association rather than a cause-and-effect relationship, it cannot determine whether problematic cannabis use contributes to suicidal thinking, whether underlying mental health difficulties contribute to both conditions, or whether other factors help explain the connection.

Nevertheless, the results point to a significant mental health concern that deserves greater recognition, particularly among people seeking help for problematic cannabis use.

Researchers Urge Greater Mental Health Screening.

One practical implication is that health care professionals should look beyond cannabis consumption itself when evaluating patients with cannabis use disorder.

Rather than focusing exclusively on depression or substance use symptoms, clinicians may benefit from asking patients directly about suicidal thoughts as part of a broader mental health assessment. This could help identify people who need additional care but whose struggles might otherwise remain unnoticed.

"Someone seeking help for cannabis use disorder may also be experiencing suicidal thoughts that are not immediately apparent," said Oyetunji. "The goal is not to assume that everyone with cannabis use disorder is suicidal but to identify those who may need additional assessment, treatment, or support.".

Recent findings suggest that the study arrives at a time when marijuana is increasingly viewed as a relatively low-risk substance. Public perceptions have shifted considerably, and negative attitudes toward cannabis have declined alongside expanding legalization and social acceptance.

However, these changes have not eliminated the mental health challenges associated with cannabis use disorder. Even though the strength of the association with suicidal thoughts did not increase over the study period, the elevated odds remained substantial.

The researchers suggest that health care providers, policymakers, and community organizations can play an important role by improving awareness, identifying vulnerable individuals, and making appropriate mental health support more accessible.

As attitudes toward marijuana continue to evolve, the findings serve as a reminder that the needs of people experiencing problematic cannabis use should remain a public health priority.

Stated Oyetunji, "As cannabis becomes more accessible and socially accepted, we should ensure that the people struggling with its use are not overlooked.".

Materials provided by Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs. Original written by W.B. Kagan. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) newly introduced years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are at the moment working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

Sources indicate that this, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Industry observers note that understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s upcoming ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we proposal for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Sources indicate that future releases, of course, include upcoming The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim presently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).

Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1190 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, an international research team has developed a newly introduced technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease.
  • Recent findings suggest that the technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain.
  • Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, an international research team has developed a newly introduced technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease. In experiments involving mice with Parkinson's-like symptoms, the approach significantly improved movement problems without requiring permanently implanted electrodes.

Recent findings suggest that the technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain. When exposed to an external magnetic field, these particles generate tiny forces that activate nearby nerve cells. Unlike conventional brain stimulation treatments, which rely on surgically implanted electrodes, the latest approach uses magnetic forces to influence brain activity. The findings, published in Advanced Science, come from researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), RWTH Aachen, and the Universities of Maastricht (the Netherlands) and Leuven (Belgium).

Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.

Parkinson's disease develops as brain cells responsible for producing dopamine gradually break down. Dopamine is a chemical messenger that plays a vital role in controlling movement. As its levels decline, communication within the brain's movement circuits becomes disrupted, contributing to tremors and other motor difficulties.

For some patients, deep brain stimulation can help control these symptoms. This treatment uses a device known as a brain pacemaker, which is implanted beneath the collarbone and connected to electrodes placed deep inside the brain. The electrodes deliver electrical stimulation to a region called the subthalamic nucleus (STN for short), helping to modify abnormal activity in the brain circuits responsible for movement.

Although this treatment can provide substantial relief, it requires a complex surgical procedure and does not work for everyone.

"The procedure is relatively complex, however, and not always successful," explains Prof. Dr. Danijela Gregurec from the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy at FAU. "This puts many Parkinson's patients off, and not all patients are suitable candidates for one of these pacemakers.".

The researchers believe magnetic stimulation could eventually provide another option, allowing doctors to influence the same deep brain structures without leaving electrodes permanently implanted.

How Tiny Magnetic Particles Stimulate Brain Cells.

The latest technology takes advantage of the ability of certain nerve cells to detect physical pressure and mechanical forces.

"We use magnetic nanoparticles that we implant in the brain," Gregurec explains. "They have a special shape and a magnetic structure. They were developed in order to transform magnetic fields into tiny mechanical forces.".

Rather than sending electrical pulses directly into the brain, the technique uses these particles to produce extremely small physical movements when a magnetic field is applied.

Industry observers note that "The traditional method establishes an electrical connection to the brain," she claims. "In contrast, we use the neurons' natural mechanosensors to influence regions deep within the brain.".

The process works by gently changing the shape of nearby nerve cell membranes. Imagine pressing a finger against an inflated balloon and creating a small indentation in its surface. The magnetic particles produce a similar effect on a microscopic scale.

This slight deformation opens specialized channels in the cell membrane that respond to mechanical pressure. Once opened, these channels allow electrically charged particles called ions to enter the nerve cells, changing their electrical activity and providing a way to stimulate the targeted brain circuits.

Magnetic Brain Stimulation Improves Movement in Mice.

To investigate whether the technology could relieve Parkinson's symptoms, the international research team conducted experiments using mice with damage to the same types of dopamine-producing nerve cells affected by the disease in humans. This damage caused movement difficulties resembling those seen in Parkinson's patients.

"Together with our partners from Maastricht, we injected magnetic nanoparticles developed here at FAU into the animals' subthalamic nucleus," Gregurec explains. "That is the very region in the brain that is also an important target for conventional deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.".

It has been revealed that the researchers used precise stereotactic injection techniques to deliver the particles to the intended location. These methods rely on carefully calculated three-dimensional coordinates to guide instruments into specific brain structures. Accurate placement was particularly important because the treatment needed to affect the correct neural circuits involved in movement.

It has been revealed that after the particles were positioned, the researchers applied an external magnetic field. The results were encouraging: the mice showed significant improvements in their movement deficits.

"The effect is roughly equivalent to what we would have expected after implanting a brain pacemaker," notes Gregurec.

The findings suggest that magnetic nanoparticles could provide a different way to achieve some of the benefits of conventional deep brain stimulation, without the need for permanently implanted electrodes.

Could Future Parkinson's Treatments Use Magnetic Headbands?

Another encouraging finding involved how the brain responded to the implanted particles over time. The magnetic nanoparticles remained in place throughout an observation period lasting several months, and the researchers found no signs of inflammation. This suggests that the particles were well tolerated during the experiments.

According to recent reports, however, delivering the particles still required an injection directly into the brain. Gregurec and her colleagues are now investigating ways to make the procedure even less invasive.

In a recent development, one possibility is to develop particles that could be injected into the bloodstream and then travel into the brain by crossing the blood-brain barrier. This protective boundary normally prevents many substances circulating in the blood from entering brain tissue. Finding a way to deliver the particles across it could eliminate the need for direct brain injections.

According to recent reports, the researchers are also exploring compact wearable devices capable of generating the magnetic fields needed for stimulation. One possibility is a headband that patients could put on themselves, potentially making treatment more convenient and adjustable.

These ideas remain at an early stage, and the researchers expect that several more years of development will be needed before the technology could be considered for clinical use.

Industry observers note that "Nevertheless, we are convinced that the new method has enormous potential," Gregurec states. "It is not only considerably simpler and cheaper than a conventional brain pacemaker, it is probably also more flexible. Adjusting the parameters of the magnetic field would allow us to control the nanoparticles more accurately.".

Beyond its potential medical applications, the technology could also become a valuable scientific tool. By allowing researchers to stimulate nerve cells through carefully controlled mechanical forces, it offers a latest way to explore how physical changes at the cellular level influence brain activity.

Although the treatment has so far been demonstrated only in animals, its ability to improve movement without permanently implanted electrodes represents a promising step toward latest approaches to Parkinson's disease and brain stimulation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 had a stellar launch, with two million XBOX players swarming to New Zealand to start their playthrough as early as possible, boasting eye-watering sales figures, and breaking viewership records.

Bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful. One GTA 6 glitch that is gathering a lot of attention is one that lets players access a first-person mode.

As expected, GTA 6 is played in third-person and although many players appreciate a first-person mode, it is absent at launch, or at least, officially.

There is a glitch that enables a first-person look. It can be a little fiddly at first, but once you get the hang of it, you will have a better view at the sights. We have all the details you need to know about how to enter first-person mode the next time you load up the game.

YouTuber OneBoyler posted a video demonstrating how to do the GTA 6 first-person glitch on PlayStation. To perform the glitch, pause the game and go to the in-game settings, under the Controller tab, scroll down until you see Touch Pad Button. Change the Touch Pad Button to Camera 2. This setting changes your touchpad from opening the map to altering your camera view.

Recent findings suggest that next, sit in the driver’s seat of a vehicle and take out your mobile phone by pressing up on the D-Pad. Put your phone away by hitting circle on a PlayStation controller and then instantly spam your touchpad button.

Recent findings suggest that once successful, you will see the world from your character’s perspective, holding the wheel of the car. From this point onward, you can safely exit the car with first-person view intact and even access your loadout. Equipping a gun allows you to hold it realistically, and the animations are compatible with first-person mode.

Bugs and glitches are just a part of modern gaming. Some can be game-breaking, others produce some funny moments, and some can actually be useful.

Recent findings suggest that also, you can drive in first-person, bringing a new level of immersion to the already gorgeous and detailed world around you. The city lights reflecting off the front of your car hit different when you’re cruising around the streets.

Industry observers note that it’s worth noting that to return to third-person mode, you must reload your save. Make sure you save at the right time and don’t make any progress you want to risk losing while experimenting with the first-person view.

When GTA 5 launched on XBOX 360 and PlayStation 3 back in 2013, a first-person mode was absent. Only when GTA 5 was ported to XBOX One, PlayStation 4, and PC did a first-person perspective arrive in the game. Included were an optional first-person cover system, a newly introduced targeting system, traditional FPS controls, and fresh animations that allowed players to see the world in a whole new way.

If history were to repeat itself, a first-person mode could be on the cards for GTA 6 in a future update. For now, if you want to explore Leonida in first-person, you’ll have to do so using the glitch.

It’s unknown what the first post-launch GTA 6 patch will entail, but if it doesn’t bring a first-person mode with it, players will be hoping that Rockstar Games decides against patching out this particular bug.

Industry News: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.
  • To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.
  • According to recent reports, studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control. These drugs also influence biological processes involved in brain function, raising questions about whether they could help preserve memory and thinking abilities.

To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.

According to recent reports, studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory. However, research involving humans has produced less consistent findings. Analyses of patient health records have found an association between GLP-1 treatment and a reduced risk of dementia among people with type 2 diabetes. These observational findings are encouraging, but they cannot determine whether the medications themselves are responsible for the lower risk.

More definitive results have also raised questions. In Novo Nordisk's EVOKE and EVOKE+ clinical trials, semaglutide failed to slow the progression of early Alzheimer's disease. Although the treatment affected several biological markers associated with Alzheimer's, those changes did not translate into a measurable slowing of the disease.

Why Weight Loss Drugs May Still Benefit the Brain.

Despite the disappointing Alzheimer's results, researchers believe GLP-1 medications could still offer cognitive benefits to certain groups of patients.

People living with obesity or type 2 diabetes sometimes experience difficulties with attention, planning, and the speed at which they process information. These cognitive problems are often associated with metabolic health and blood vessel function, suggesting they may respond differently to treatment than the changes caused by Alzheimer's disease.

Improving blood sugar regulation, metabolism, or vascular health could potentially help preserve cognitive abilities, even if the same medications cannot slow an established neurodegenerative disease.

Stina Börchers, the review's first author and a researcher affiliated with both the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen, emphasizes the need to determine whether starting treatment earlier could make a difference.

According to recent reports, "We need to find out whether these treatments can help people with obesity or diabetes preserve their cognitive abilities, particularly if treatment begins before cognitive problems become established. It is also notable to identify which patients might benefit," says Stina Börchers.

Unlocking New Treatments to Protect Memory.

It has been revealed that A central unanswered question is how GLP-1 medications might influence the brain. Their potential cognitive effects could result from improvements in metabolic health, direct actions within the brain, or a combination of both.

Understanding these mechanisms could help researchers identify which patients are most likely to benefit and potentially lead to medications designed specifically to support memory and other thinking abilities.

Christoffer Clemmensen, the review's senior author and a research group leader at the University of Copenhagen, sees an opportunity to use increasingly advanced obesity treatments to explore the connection between metabolism and the brain.

"Obesity medicines are becoming increasingly sophisticated, offering new opportunities to understand how metabolic regulation influences brain function. By disentangling the direct and indirect effects of these drugs on the brain, we may ultimately be able to develop treatments specifically aimed at preserving cognitive function," says Christoffer Clemmensen.

The researchers are calling for clinical trials that evaluate memory, attention, and other cognitive abilities beginning when patients first start treatment. Following these changes over time could help establish whether GLP-1 drugs genuinely protect brain function and clarify who might benefit most.

Sources indicate that they also stress that treatment is not without potential drawbacks, particularly for older adults and people who are physically frail. Rapid weight loss can lead to a reduction in muscle mass, which may weaken physical function and offset some of the possible benefits.

Careful monitoring will therefore be essential as researchers investigate whether today's weight loss and diabetes medications could eventually provide newly introduced ways to protect the brain.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with latest threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj.

Recent findings suggest that what we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension enhancement is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

According to recent reports, similar to other Bonus Paths, the fresh Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several newly introduced customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

This remarkable new material could solve a major carbon capture problem

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor.
  • The researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs.
  • The advance could have key implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor. Instead of allowing moisture to interfere with the process, the material uses it to help maintain effective carbon capture.

The researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. Their findings, published in Angewandte Chemie, could help make carbon capture more practical and affordable for factories and other industrial facilities.

The advance could have key implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Industrial operations, including the burning of fossil fuels to produce energy, are major sources of atmospheric carbon dioxide. In the United States, industry accounts for 30% of total greenhouse gas emissions, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

A New Material That Overcomes a Major Carbon Capture Problem.

It has been revealed that the latest material, called BVR-X, has an unusual internal structure that keeps water and carbon dioxide largely separated within its microscopic pores. By directing the two substances into different regions, it prevents water molecules from occupying the spaces needed to capture carbon dioxide.

"This internal organization helps the material work under conditions that more closely resemble real industrial emissions," mentioned Kyriakos Stylianou, professor of chemistry in the OSU College of Science.

Sources indicate that MOFs are crystalline materials built from positively charged metal ions connected by organic molecules called ligands, which act as linkers. The metal ions form connection points, or nodes, while the linkers join them together into repeating structures resembling tiny cages. These structures contain extremely small pores that can trap gas molecules on their internal surfaces through a process called adsorption, much like a sponge holds substances within its structure.

Recent findings suggest that one of the advantages of MOFs is their remarkable adaptability. Scientists can combine different metals and organic linkers to create materials with specific characteristics. According to Stylianou, millions of MOF designs are theoretically possible. Researchers have already synthesized more than 100,000 distinct MOFs and predicted the properties of hundreds of thousands more.

Why Carbon Capture Needs Better Materials.

It has been revealed that "The capture of CO2 is critical for meeting net-zero emission targets," stated Stylianou, who directs OSU's Materials Discovery Laboratory, known as the MaD Lab. "MOFs have shown a lot of promise because of their porosity and their structural versatility.".

According to recent reports, carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas released when fossil fuels are burned. As it accumulates in the atmosphere, it traps heat and contributes to global warming.

According to recent reports, one approach to addressing the problem involves removing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Facilities designed for this purpose are beginning to operate in different parts of the world. The world's largest such plant opened in Iceland in 2024, although its annual carbon removal capacity is still relatively small compared with global emissions. According to Stylianou, the facility can capture roughly as much carbon dioxide in one year as about 7,200 cars produce over the same period.

It has been revealed that capturing carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere is another option, and the technologies used for this purpose are considerably more established. At factories and power plants, carbon capture systems can intercept emissions as they travel through exhaust systems and smokestacks. Some of these systems use MOFs to adsorb carbon dioxide molecules from the passing gases.

How Water Makes Industrial Carbon Capture Difficult.

According to recent reports, A major obstacle, however, is that industrial exhaust often contains substantial amounts of water vapor. Many MOFs that perform well in controlled laboratory experiments lose much of their carbon capture ability when exposed to the humid conditions found in actual smokestacks.

According to recent reports, the gases can be dried before carbon dioxide is removed, but doing so requires additional equipment and energy. Those costs can become so significant that the overall process is no longer economically practical for industrial use.

In a recent development, BVR-X offers a different approach. Rather than requiring moisture to be removed, the material responds to water in a way that preserves its ability to collect carbon dioxide. Its internal organization allows water and carbon dioxide to occupy different regions, helping prevent the competition that normally undermines carbon capture performance.

Sources indicate that "Water usually makes capturing carbon dioxide more difficult," he said. "Our newly introduced material does something unusual: It responds to water by changing in a way that lets it keep capturing CO2 effectively even under very humid conditions.".

Strong Performance Under Realistic Industrial Conditions.

Laboratory tests demonstrated that BVR-X could efficiently capture carbon dioxide from a highly humid gas stream containing only 4% carbon dioxide.

Recent findings suggest that that concentration is particularly relevant to emissions from burning natural gas, where carbon dioxide makes up a relatively small proportion of the exhaust. Extracting it becomes especially difficult when large quantities of water vapor are also present.

The experiments therefore tested the material under conditions that resemble an notable real-world challenge, "where separating a small amount of CO2 in the presence of substantial water is particularly challenging," stated Stylianou.

The researchers also found that BVR-X could repeatedly capture and release carbon dioxide without losing its effectiveness over dozens of cycles. This ability to regenerate the material is key because commercial carbon capture systems must reuse their capture materials many times to keep operating costs manageable.

Recent findings suggest that "And the material can be regenerated and reused, maintaining performance through dozens of capture-and-release cycles and tolerating demanding conditions," he added. "Those are important qualities for practical carbon-capture technologies.".

The results suggest that BVR-X could help overcome a major limitation of existing MOF technologies, particularly in industrial settings where removing moisture from exhaust gases would otherwise be costly.

In a recent development, the study brought together researchers from several institutions. Stylianou worked with MaD Lab members Ankit Yadav, Emmanuel Musa and Andrzej Gładysiak, along with Micah Hickethier, Chun-Wai Chang and Kai Shen Choong from the Oregon State College of Engineering.

Additional collaborators included scientists from the University of California, Berkeley; the University of Oregon; and the ARAMCO Research and Development Center.

Funding was provided by Saudi Aramco, the Murdock Charitable Trust, and a donor-advised fund established by Oregon State University alumni and retired public school teachers Brian and Marilyn Kleiner through the OSU Foundation.

Materials provided by Oregon State University. Original written by Steve Lundeberg. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
